subject: Banking
title: Why Checks Still Exist
description: A micro-lesson that makes Why Checks Still Exist usable.

hook.text: Americans still write 3.6 billion checks per year. In a world of instant payments, paper checks refuse to die.

buildup.text: Businesses use checks for large payments because they create a paper trail.

discovery.text: Checks give the payer control over timing. You write the check today but the money moves later. That float is valuable.

twist.text: Younger generations barely use checks. Usage drops 7% per year. Within a decade, checks may become niche instruments.

climax.text: Checks persist because they serve specific business needs that digital alternatives have not fully replaced yet.

punchline.text: 3.6 billion checks yearly, declining 7% annually. Slow death.

quiz.question: Why do businesses still prefer checks for some payments?
options: They create a paper trail and offer payer control over timing
